title: DDL and Schema Management
description: Modify database structure with ALTER TABLE, manage schemas, rename objects, drop database objects, and create synonyms for abstraction.

data.text: So far you have focused on reading and writing data. But databases change over time — new columns are needed, tables are renamed, stale objects are dropped. Data Definition Language (DDL) handles these structural changes. This lesson covers the most common DDL operations.
ALTER TABLE — add, alter, and drop columns
ALTER TABLE modifies the structure of an existing table. The three most common sub-operations are ADD (new column), ALTER (change type/nullability), and DROP COLUMN (remove).

data.title: Add a column
data.code:
ALTER TABLE production.products
ADD    discontinued BIT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

Drop a column
ALTER TABLE is expensive on large tables
data.text: Adding or dropping columns on a large table can lock it for seconds or minutes. Schedule these operations during maintenance windows, and test the impact first on a copy.

A schema is a named container for database objects — a way to group related tables, views, and procedures. It provides an additional namespace so you can have, for example, both Sales.Customers and Archive.Customers in the same database.

sp_rename syntax
sp_rename has side effects
data.text: sp_rename updates metadata only, not application code. If your application hard-codes the old table name, it will break. Renaming is generally discouraged — design the right name upfront.
DROP removes a database object permanently. Use IF EXISTS (SQL Server 2016+) to avoid errors when the object doesn't exist. DROP TABLE is more efficient than DELETE for removing all rows.

data.title: DROP with IF EXISTS

data.text: A synonym is an alias for a database object. It lets you reference a table, view, stored procedure, or function by a simpler name — and it becomes invaluable when you need to rename or move an object without recompiling dependent applications.

data.title: Creating and using a synonym
When to use synonyms
data.text: Synonyms solve two problems: they shorten long multi-part names (server.database.schema.object → orders), and they provide backward compatibility when you rename a table — existing code continues to work through the old name.

data.title: DDL essentials
points: ALTER TABLE ADD / ALTER COLUMN / DROP COLUMN changes table structure
CREATE SCHEMA and ALTER SCHEMA ... TRANSFER organize objects into named containers
sp_rename changes an object's name but not your application code
DROP TABLE is faster than DELETE for clearing all rows — use IF EXISTS to be safe
Synonyms alias objects for simpler names and rename-safe compatibility
